A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that for any constant p}<1, any constant number of hops h, and any constant number f of faulty links, we can construct layouts in K n with congestion O(logn), which tolerate all existing faulty links with probability at least 1-p.
we give upper and low bounds on the congestion of 1 and h hop f-tolerant virtual path layouts in K n and construct layouts that achieve these bounds, for any f and h.
we have obtained upper bounds on congestion which are within a constant factor of the best possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the problem of constructing layouts that tolerate faults is closely related to the diameter problem for the network Kn[\mathcal{F}] and that a good understanding of the diameter of this network leads to efficient algorithms for constructing layouts.
the congestion of a layout can be made to be a very weak function of f, the number of faulty links.
the congestion of f-tolerant ATM layouts can be bounded by a function of the number of faulty links, rather than by a function of n.
